top_story.headline: Army hands eleven firms a place on a $4.17 billion contract to build and modernize its ammunition plants
top_story.dek: The Army Contracting Command at Rock Island, Illinois, made multiple awards on November 5 for design, build and commissioning work at seven government-owned, contractor-operated ammunition plants.
paragraphs: The U.S. Army Contracting Command – Rock Island says it awarded 11 indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity multiple-award task order contracts from solicitation W519TC26RA020. The base ordering period is five years (1,826 calendar days). The winners will compete for task orders covering design, build, facility modernization and commissioning at seven government-owned, contractor-operated Army ammunition plants. The notice names Holston (Kingsport, Tennessee), Iowa (Middletown, Iowa), Lake City (Independence, Missouri), Milan (Milan, Tennessee), the Quad City Cartridge Case Facility (Rock Island, Illinois) and Radford among them.

The eleven awardees are Bering-Weston JV, LLC, Hensel Phelps Construction Co, Clark Construction Group LLC, MSM Group North America Inc., Applied Research Associates, Inc., Parsons Government Services Inc., M. C. Dean, Inc., J Kokolakis Contracting Inc, BAE Systems Ordnance Systems Inc., Alberici Constructors Inc and Burns & McDonnell Engineering Company, Inc. Each of the eleven notices lists the same figure, $4,171,491,000, dated November 5, 2026. Because the figure is identical across all eleven, it appears to be a shared program ceiling, not a separate award to each firm.
The one attached file has not been read yet; it is queued for a later edition, so the per-plant scope and any per-firm limits are not yet confirmed.

sections.headline: Federal Retirement Thrift Investment Board plans a no-bid deal with Washington's transit authority to run its employees' transit subsidies
paragraphs: Nine items were tagged to Washington, D.C.: one sole-source justification (posted as a Special Notice), two solicitations, one special notice, four sources-sought notices and one USAspending award. A Treasury staffing notice that only mentions a D.C.-based post moved back to Solicitations, and three notices already listed in earlier editions (a General Services Administration garage at St. Elizabeths, a Senate software purchase and a State Department staffing notice) were left out.

blocks.title: Federal Retirement Thrift Investment Board plans a no-bid deal with Washington's transit authority to run its employees' transit subsidies
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: The Federal Retirement Thrift Investment Board intends to buy access to the SmartBenefits program for administering transit subsidies for its employees, a sole-source buy under the small-purchase authority (FAR 13.106-1(b)). It says the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority is the sole owner, operator and administrator of SmartBenefits, the transit benefit system used throughout the National Capital Region. The notice was posted as a Special Notice, no value is stated, and only the notice text was available. The pipeline logged an earlier sole-source notice for the same program from a Homeland Security Department component.

sections.headline: Marine Corps buys 15 intelligence shelters from Anduril without competition, citing the company's prototype work
paragraphs: 38 new justifications appear here; 20 of the day's justifications were posted under other notice types, and one repeat from an earlier edition was left out. Four are worth a full read, and seven Veterans Affairs picture-archive refreshes from one vendor are grouped below.

blocks.text: Must read

blocks.title: Marine Corps buys 15 intelligence shelters from Anduril without competition, citing the company's prototype work
meta: only one company can do it
Department of the Navy, Marine Corps Systems Command
blocks.text: The Marine Corps Systems Command program office for intelligence and cyberspace operations will place a sole-source delivery order under Anduril's existing Army single-award contract for 15 expeditionary shelters (8 operator, 7 processing) and logistics support for the Maritime Targeting Cell. The justification says Anduril is the only known source able to deliver in time, after the Marine Corps Warfighting Laboratory funded a 2024-2026 prototype with the company. A separate analysis notes that other vendors build shielded, towable enclosures but only Anduril holds the proprietary designs for this configuration. The value is redacted.

blocks.title: Fish and Wildlife Service picks a local septic company for a no-bid well because local drillers won't register on SAM.gov
blocks.text: The agency needs to replace a failing circa-1950 well at the headquarters of the Eastern Virginia Rivers refuge complex. The justification says local drillers gave only two verbal quotes ($18,000 and $25,000), that two solicitations in 2026 drew six outside bids of roughly four to five times the local estimates, and that local contractors consider SAM.gov registration "too onerous." It claims savings of over $50,000 versus those bids and notes the company drilled a well on the refuge about 11 years ago.

blocks.title: Air Force plans to modernize Lackland's base-defense security system through Johnson Controls without competition, while admitting other vendors could do it
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center intends a bilateral sole-source modification to modernize the Integrated Base Defense Security System at Lackland Air Force Base, including hardware, software, design and installation. The notice says market research "confirms that multiple vendors possess the ability," but the company is the only one that can do it without unacceptable delay and duplicated cost because it is already doing on-site sustainment there. Capability statements are due by email at 3:00 PM Eastern on November 20, 2026. It was posted as a Special Notice.

The justification says the company holds all the fabrication drawings, patterns and manufacturing and overhaul procedures and has been the supplier since the Space Shuttle program.

sections.headline: Army's Redstone Arsenal wastewater contract extended a year without competition, approved after the fact
paragraphs: Four new extensions or bridges today: the Redstone Arsenal wastewater contract, a one-year Air Force software-platform bridge, a six-month Office of Personnel Management data support extension and a military billing extension.

blocks.title: Army's Redstone Arsenal wastewater contract extended a year without competition, approved after the fact
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
blocks.text: Defense Logistics Agency Energy extends the privatized wastewater utility contract at Redstone Arsenal, Alabama, which expires November 9, 2026, by 12 months to November 9, 2027. The justification says it was "approved and publicized after award," and blames unanticipated delays in the novation process and the complexity of the 10-year follow-on contract. The company owns the wastewater system; the Army will cover fiscal year 2027 funding, and the existing monthly rate holds for six months before price adjustments begin.

blocks.title: Air Force gives its Platform One Party Bus software platform a one-year no-bid bridge
meta: Vendor redacted in the public copy
urgent need, no time to compete
blocks.text: The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center approved a one-year sole-source bridge for operations and sustainment of the Party Bus DevSecOps platform, saying a non-incumbent would need time to recruit and clear staff and gain access to government systems. The justification says the government keeps unlimited data rights and that the platform is built on open-source frameworks.

blocks.title: Office of Personnel Management extends Excella's data support for federal personnel records six months without competition

blocks.text: Through the General Services Administration's centralized acquisition office, the personnel agency modifies Excella's call order for 30 full-time staff supporting the eOPF, HRLOB and EHRI systems, for December 7, 2026 to June 6, 2027. The justification says switching vendors mid-stream while the work moves into the governmentwide Core HCM project would create unacceptable risk.

footer.coverage_window: SAM.gov notices posted November 5-6, 2026; USAspending actions through early November 2026 with a trailing sweep, plus the Defense Department's 90-day-delayed releases; late document findings from files posted in August through October 2026.
footer.sources: OMB apportionment data via openomb.org and apportionment-public.max.gov; USAspending.gov API; SAM.gov contract opportunities and their attached documents.
footer.known_gaps: J&A extraction failed for two justifications (the Muskogee and Grand Junction Veterans Affairs imaging notices), which were judged from titles and award data. The OMB apportionments pass found no flagged files and reported no gaps. Document coverage: about 2,467 attachments on 503 notices were identified and roughly 480 were read; 1,914 are queued for later editions, 29 are access-restricted on SAM.gov and 44 could not be downloaded or read (10,576 files overall are queued). About 1,600 links to outside portals (mostly DIBBS) were not followed.
